t: You're at Bunhill Fields, a former burial ground just north of the City of London. About 1.6 hectares remain, mostly a public garden kept by the City of London Corporation. Several of the people buried here were writers and thinkers outside the established church. William Blake, poet and artist, lived in London almost all his life and lies here. Daniel Defoe, author of Robinson Crusoe, is buried here, and so is John Bunyan, who wrote The Pilgrim's Progress. George Fox, a founder of the Quakers, is also here. So are Thomas Newcomen, who created the atmospheric engine in 1712, and Thomas Bayes, whose name is on Bayes' theorem.
